research_rationale: Executive Order 11851 of April 10, 1975 (40 FR 16645), Delegation of Authority To Issue Regulations Limiting Imports of Certain Cheeses, is issued under section 204 of the Agricultural Act of 1956, as amended (7 U.S.C. 1854), and 3 U.S.C. 301. Section 1 authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury, with the concurrence of the Secretary of State and the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations, to implement an agreement concluded in December 1974 with the Commission of the European Communities by issuing regulations (a) preventing importation into the Customs Territory of the United States, except Puerto Rico, of certain European Communities cheeses on which restitution payments have been made for export to Puerto Rico, other possessions or any country other than the United States, and (b) preventing importation of such cheeses into Puerto Rico for transshipment elsewhere in the Customs Territory. Section 2 authorizes heads of departments and agencies to redelegate, with the Treasury regulation-issuing function redelegable only to officials appointed by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, as 3 U.S.C. 301 provides. The packet's machine inventory merged section 2 into subsection (b) and left a fragment '301.' as a fourth clause, so I corrected the inventory into four clauses with absolute character spans in the held original text (section 1 lead-in and recital, subsection (a), subsection (b), section 2). Search of held texts for the number EO 11851 finds only the order, the 1989 OFR codification (no amendment or revocation) and 19 CFR 12.6; the OFR catalog record has no disposition note; the bounded searches report only machine hits for the U.S. Code note and 19 CFR 12.6, none of which ends or amends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. The held text of 19 CFR 12.6 (eCFR searched point-in-time as of 2026-10-14) names the order. The order's own text states no end date, event or condition; the December 1974 agreement is its purpose, not a condition of its continuance, and no held source shows that agreement ended. All four clauses are operative as of 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: No clause is terminated, so no savings or residual question arises; the delegation and redelegation authority continue, and no regulation issued under it is claimed as a residual of an ended command.
earlier_end_check: The order states no end date, event or condition; held texts naming EO 11851 (the order, the 1989 codification and 19 CFR 12.6) record no earlier revocation, supersession or amendment, and the OFR catalog has no disposition note.
scope_check: Corrected inventory: section 1 lead-in with the authority recital, subsection (a), subsection (b) and section 2 together cover the whole operative text from the recital to the signature line; the machine fragment '301.' was part of section 2 and is no longer a separate clause.
independent_command_check: Subsections (a) and (b) are separate authorizations to issue regulations (entry into the Customs Territory except Puerto Rico; entry into Puerto Rico for transshipment) and section 2 is a separate redelegation rule; each is decided on its own and none has an end of its own.
savings_check: No clause ended, so there is nothing to save; no residual effect is claimed.

research_rationale: Executive Order 13276 of November 15, 2002 (67 FR 69985), Delegation of Responsibilities Concerning Undocumented Aliens Interdicted or Intercepted in the Caribbean Region, issued under sections 212(f) and 215(a)(1) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1182(f), 1185(a)(1)) and 3 U.S.C. 301, assigns duties for undocumented aliens interdicted in the Caribbean region: section 1(a) custody and screening (originally the Attorney General) with a facility possibly at Guantanamo Bay, 1(b) the Secretary of State on persons in need of protection and resettlement, 1(c) the Secretary of Defense on facilities and, in a mass migration, support; section 2 defines mass migration; section 3 contains scope and general provisions. The 14-clause machine inventory covers the whole text from the preamble to section 3(e) and I confirmed it is complete; I corrected it to 13 clauses by merging the 14-character section 3 heading into section 3(a), and the entries 'lead' (the authority recital) and 'sec1' (the lead-in to section 1) are not commands but frame the commands and are carried as operative with the order. The one amending order found is EO 13286 (February 28, 2003, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92), section 1, which replaces the Attorney General with the Secretary of Homeland Security wherever it appears in section 1; the OFR catalog record for EO 13276 lists no 'Amended by' note and instead reads 'See: EO 12807, May 24, 1992 | Amends: EO 13286, February 28, 2003'; EO 13286 was signed after EO 13276 and its section 1 amends EO 13276, so I read that catalog note as a transposed record of the EO 13286 amendment, not as a second instrument. EO 12807 (Interdiction of Illegal Aliens) is referred to in sections 1(c)(ii) and 3(a) and is not a revocation or amendment of this order. Search of held texts for the number EO 13276 finds the order, EO 13286, the Federal Register copies of those two, 32 CFR 245.9 (which lists EO 13286 as amending EO 13276), two Federal Register copies of Cuba-policy presidential memoranda (the National Security Presidential Memorandum published at 82 FR 48875, October 20, 2017, and the Memorandum of June 30, 2025, 90 FR 38913) that each state they do not affect EO 13276; none revokes or supersedes the order. The bounded searches report machine hits (the OFR catalog entries, the text of EO 13286 and the U.S. Code note), none of which revokes, supersedes or ends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. The 8 U.S.C. 1182 note prints the order as amended. The order's own text has no end date; the 'until' phrases in section 1(a)(ii) set how long the custody duty lasts for a particular alien, not an end of the clause. The order is operative as of 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: No clause is terminated, so no savings or residual question arises; EO 13286 section 1 amended the clauses and the clauses continue as amended.
earlier_end_check: The order states no end date, event or condition; the held amending order only substitutes the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Attorney General; no held instrument revokes or supersedes EO 13276 and the OFR catalog record has no revocation note.
scope_check: Corrected inventory of 13 clauses (the machine section 3 heading merged into section 3(a)) covers the preamble, section 1(a) to (c), section 2 and section 3(a) to (e); I read the whole held text and found no command outside them; the two non-command entries (recital and section 1 lead-in) are carried with the order and are not separate commands.
independent_command_check: Section 1(a), 1(b) and 1(c) assign separate duties to the Secretary of Homeland Security (formerly the Attorney General), the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense; section 1(a)(ii) screening is a separate discretionary power and its 'until' wording governs how long custody lasts for an alien; section 2 is a definition and section 3 contains scope clauses. Each is decided separately and none has its own end.
savings_check: No clause ended; the amendment continued the clauses as amended under the owner ruling on strike-and-insert amendments, and no residual under superseded wording is claimed.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12109 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1067), Federal Physicians Comparability Allowance, has two numbered sections in the held Federal Register text. Section 1-101 designates and empowers the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, to exercise the President's authority under 5 U.S.C. 5948 to prescribe regulations, criteria and conditions for comparability allowances for certain Federal physicians. Section 1-102 provides that until OPM is established (on or before January 1, 1979) under Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 the Civil Service Commission exercises that authority. The packet's single whole clause covered both, so I corrected the inventory into two clauses with absolute character spans in the held original text: 1-101 operative, 1-102 terminated by its own terms. The held text of EO 12107 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12107.txt, section 1-101) states that the establishment of OPM under Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 is effective January 1, 1979; that is the date on which the until-OPM-is-established condition occurred and the transitional command to the Civil Service Commission ended, by the order's own terms. EO 12107 does not amend EO 12109 and is cited only as the source of the date. Search of held texts for the number EO 12109 finds only the order and 5 CFR part 595 (authority citation); the OFR catalog record has no disposition note; the bounded searches report no machine hit that ends or amends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. 5 U.S.C. 5948 note prints the order's text as current, including section 1-102 as historical text. The held text of 5 U.S.C. 5948 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s5948.txt) is in the Code with no sunset provision, and the eCFR search (point-in-time as of 2026-10-14) finds 5 CFR part 595 (physicians' comparability allowances), whose authority citation names E.O. 12109. Section 1-101 is therefore operative as of 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: Section 1-102 ended on January 1, 1979 when OPM was established; it was a transitional allocation of the same delegated authority to the Civil Service Commission, and no action under it needs saving beyond what the continuing delegation in 1-101 and 5 CFR part 595 already govern. No claim is made that any residual duty under 1-102 survives.
earlier_end_check: Section 1-101 has no end date, event or condition and no held instrument ends it. Section 1-102 ends by its own terms when OPM was established, which the held text of EO 12107 dates to January 1, 1979; no earlier establishment date appears in held texts (EO 12107 makes the Reorganization Plan's establishment effective on that day).
scope_check: Corrected inventory: 1-101 (preamble and designation) and 1-102 (transitional clause) cover the entire held operative text from the authority recital to the signature line, so no command is outside the two clauses.
independent_command_check: The designation of the OPM Director in 1-101 is independent of the Civil Service Commission's transitional exercise in 1-102: 1-102 ended on its own terms on January 1, 1979 while 1-101 continues, so the two are tracked separately.
savings_check: The only ended command is the transitional exercise by the Civil Service Commission, which no longer exists; 5 U.S.C. 5948 and 5 CFR part 595 continue under the 1-101 delegation, so no residual under 1-102 is claimed.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12572 of November 3, 1986 (51 FR 40401), Relations With the Northern Mariana Islands, is one operative sentence in the held Federal Register text: consistent with the Covenant approved by Pub. L. 94-241, the relations of the United States with the Government of the Northern Mariana Islands, in matters not the program responsibility of another Federal department or agency, are placed under the general administrative supervision of the Secretary of the Interior. The held original text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12572.txt) names the order number, date and subject, and the whole order is verified in the packet. Search of held texts for the number EO 12572 finds only the order itself and the 1989 OFR codification (which records no amendment or revocation); the OFR catalog record has no disposition note; the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog report no machine hit that ends or amends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. The 48 U.S.C. 1801 note prints the same sentence as current text with the label provided. The eCFR search was point-in-time as of 2026-10-14 and found no regulation naming the order. The order's own text has no end date, event or condition; the term-signal records attached to the packet for this order come from the text of the Covenant (48 U.S.C. 1801) and its notes, not from the order, and do not state an end for this command. The order is therefore operative as of 2026-10-14 and was not revoked or superseded on the held evidence.
savings_reason: No clause is terminated, so no savings or residual question arises; the order has no later amendment, revocation or supersession on the held evidence, and nothing it did is left as an exhausted command.
earlier_end_check: The order's own text states no date, event or condition for ending; held texts naming EO 12572 (only itself and the 1989 codification) record no earlier revocation, supersession or amendment; the Covenant-derived term records in the packet are not terms of this order.
scope_check: The held text is a single operative sentence and the packet inventory has one clause, whole, covering all of it; the clause is complete and no clause was added or removed.
independent_command_check: The sentence contains one command (general administrative supervision by the Secretary of the Interior of relations with the Government of the Northern Mariana Islands, subject to other agencies' program responsibility); there is no separate command that could end on its own.
savings_check: No clause ended, so there is nothing to save; no residual effect is claimed.

research_rationale: Executive Order 8809 of June 28, 1941 (6 FR 3209), Good Conduct Medal, is a single operative paragraph in the held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8809.txt; trailing number [No. 8809], signed Franklin D. Roosevelt at The White House June 28, 1941): a Good Conduct Medal is established and may be awarded, under regulations of the Secretary of War, to enlisted men of the Army of the United States who hereafter honorably complete three years of active Federal military service and are recommended by their commanding officers. Three later orders each amend that single clause and are recorded as later events with before and after text: EO 9323 (March 31, 1943) restated the paragraph; EO 10444 (April 10, 1953) restated it again; and EO 14085, section 2 (October 3, 2022) struck and inserted words. The OFR catalog record for EO 8809 reads 'Amended by: EO 9323, March 31, 1943; EO 10444, April 10, 1953 | See: Transfer Order 30 of the Secretary of Defense dated December 10, 1948 (13 FR 8163)'. Both Amended by notes are addressed as later events. The See note is a cross reference to a Secretary of Defense transfer order whose text is not held; it is not a revocation note, it predates EO 10444 (which already names the Secretary of the Air Force), and I do not treat it as ending or changing the order. EO 14085, which the catalog does not list, is found in held texts and in the U.S. Code note. Search of held texts for the number EO 8809 finds the order, EO 9323, EO 10444 (and the duplicate page text under EO 10445 and EO 9324), EO 14085 and the 1989 codification; none revokes or supersedes the order. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog report machine hits (the OFR catalog amendment notes for EO 9323 and EO 10444, the text of EO 14085, and the U.S. Code note), none of which revokes, supersedes or ends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 note prints the order as amended by EO 9323, EO 10444 and EO 14085 section 2, as current text; the printed current text matches the text as restated by EO 10444 and amended by EO 14085. The order's own text states no end date or condition. Substance changed across the restatements; a reviewer should read the before and after wording in the later events. The clause is operative as of 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: No clause is terminated, so no savings or residual question arises. The 1941 and 1943 wording is superseded by the later restatements as amendments, not ends; awards made under earlier wording are not claimed as residual effects of an exhausted command.
earlier_end_check: The order states no end date, event or condition. The later orders restate or amend it but none revokes or supersedes it or ends the medal; the OFR See note naming Transfer Order 30 is a cross reference without held text and predates the 1953 restatement. No earlier end appears in held texts naming EO 8809.
scope_check: The held original is one paragraph and the packet inventory has one clause, whole, covering all of it; I confirmed the text is complete from the order heading through the signature and number. The later restatements amend the same single clause, so no clause is added or lost.
independent_command_check: The paragraph establishes the medal and authorizes awards under regulations; the proviso in later wording (no award for less than one year except for disability) is part of the same award authorization, not an independent command that could end on its own.
savings_check: No clause ended; amendments continue the clause as amended under the owner ruling on strike-and-insert amendments, and no residual under superseded wording is claimed.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11298 of August 14, 1966 (31 FR 10915), Prescribing the Interest Rate for Deposit of Savings of Members of the Uniformed Services, prescribes under section 1035 of title 10, U.S. Code, as amended by the Act of August 14, 1966, that amounts deposited by members of the uniformed services under that section accrue interest at ten percent per annum, compounded quarterly, effective September 1, 1966. The packet text is bounded to the target clause envelope because the heading was not segmented, but the held Federal Register page text (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_11298.txt) carries the heading Executive Order 11298, Prescribing the Interest Rate for Deposit of Savings of Members of the Uniformed Services, directly above the paragraph, and the order has no other paragraph. Search of held texts for the number EO 11298 finds only the order and the 1989 OFR codification; the OFR catalog record has no disposition note; the bounded searches report no machine hit that ends or amends it. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. 10 U.S.C. 1035 note prints the order as current text. The held text of 10 U.S.C. 1035(b) (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t10-s1035.txt) still provides that interest at a rate prescribed by the President, not to exceed 10 percent a year, accrues on amounts deposited, so the statute the order implements remains in force and the prescribed rate equals its ceiling. The sentence on September 1, 1966 is a start date, not an end. The term-signal records attached to the packet for this order come from the statute's notes (Pub. L. 89-538 and Pub. L. 90-122) and concern deposits and payments, not the rate prescribed by this order. The order is operative as of 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: No clause is terminated, so no savings or residual question arises; the rate prescription continues and no later order or statute supplies a different rate on the held evidence.
earlier_end_check: The order states no end date, event or condition (its only date is the September 1, 1966 effective date); held texts naming EO 11298 record no earlier revocation, supersession or amendment; the statute-derived term records are not terms of this order.
scope_check: The order is a single paragraph with one operative command and one effective-date sentence; the packet inventory has one clause, whole, covering both, and I confirmed it is complete against the held page text.
independent_command_check: There is one command, a ten percent per annum rate compounded quarterly for deposits under section 1035; the effective-date sentence only dates its start and is not an independent command.
savings_check: No clause ended, so there is nothing to save; no residual effect is claimed.
